opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kimberly Dennis (employee ID E010) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E010.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full_time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not allowed. Max for full_time without owning role is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin to Source Code, which exceeds max of read. Recommend read.
reason: Kimberly Dennis (E010) requested admin to Source Code. HR (authoritative for employment type/role) verifies she is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by Engineer, and Payroll Specialist does not own it, so admin is not allowed for this employee; per policy, full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system. The requested admin exceeds the maximum of write, so the maximum (write) is granted. (The Security note lists her as contractor with basic training, which would cap at read; however, employment type is an HR fact, and under the verified full-time status the allowed maximum is write. Either way, admin is denied.)

- contractor: read, or write if advanced training. Never admin. Security training is basic, so max read.
